newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday due to new domestic A share issues and listings early this week, which sucked funds out of the market, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 11.20 percent from 11.00 percent last Friday.
Turnover surged to 9.57 million lots from 4.64 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Many securities houses and brokerages borrowed on the repo market to trade on the A share market," said one trader. "The trend is likely to continue in the next few days."
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Monday, with funds flowing out to rising A share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen, traders said.
But the most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, regarded as a barometer of the spot market, closed up at 123.90 yuan from 123.47, boosted by a new bond issue early next month.
The Finance Ministry has said it will issue 20 billion yuan worth of seven-year T-bonds starting early November.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 2.79 million lots from 1.54 million.
